newsitem.title: USA: Northwest says gas compressor out for 2 wks.
newsitem.headline: Northwest says gas compressor out for 2 wks.

text.p: Northwest Pipeline said Tuesday that its Chehalis gas compressor station in southwestern Washington will be shut Wednesday for about two weeks.
As a result of the outage, supplies will be cut by about 130 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) out of a total current capacity of 620 mmcfd.
The unit is being taken out of service due to "an unacceptable level of vibration, movement and knocking," a company letter to shippers noted.
The unscheduled maintenance will include "engine realignment, cylinder support repair, and the replacement of all power piston carrier bushings," the letter also stated.
Spot gas prices at Sumas, Wash., fell more than 10 cents today to $1.23-1.31 per million British thermal units due to the outage, market sources said.
Northwest is a subsidiary of the Williams Cos.
